text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool error affecting tenant AcmeCorp (vpc-acme-01). 503s observed on inference router; error spike began ~1713103500. Auto-escalation to on-call.

miguel: ack, I'm on it. Seeing repeated `KV cache` OOMs in the acme dedicated pool. Router shows `503 gateway` + `tenant io timeout` on a subset of pods. Impact looks contained to their dedicated nodes, not shared runtime.

miguel: quick note — to investigate we need a full set of request/response logs for the window 1713103200-1713103700. Our retention policy redacts PII and dewaf rules block exporting raw logs for enterprise VPCs without legal signoff. pinging legal.

sarah: miguel — I'm the handoff in 15m. if you need me to take the page, call me. Also @anya please confirm whether Acme has requested we pull raw traces for their auditors.

anya: confirmed. Acme has an ongoing audit and requested a raw trace extract for this incident. They expect full headers (including masked user identifiers) and correlation ids. They understand we need a redaction exception but want minimal delay.

miguel: copying the log snippet I can see (redacted inline). this is what we see from the router for a failing request:

```
[2024-04-14T09:15:11Z] tenant=acme request_id=rid-abc123 user_email=[REDACTED_EMAIL] model=gpt-x status=503 error="kv_cache_oom"
```

miguel: the actual logs include unredacted user_email and originating IP. Legal: can we get an emergency redaction exception to extract logs to an encrypted, short-lived store? Need to reproduce and mitigate.

jane-legal: @miguel @sarah thanks for the ping. We can approve a narrowly-scoped exception if the following controls are in place:
- export to a customer-specific, access-restricted S3 bucket (redwood-incidents-acme-exception)
- server-side KMS encryption with restricted IAM (only on-call + legal)
- TTL 48 hours max, auto-delete
- automated redaction pass (email -> <email_redacted>, ip -> <ip_redacted>) before long-term storage
- signed exception form from Acme security + Redwood CISO
I need a justification note (what fields, why needed, who will access).

alex-ciso: +1 to Jane. Also require a security review of the extraction script. If any raw PII must be seen by humans, minimal number (2) people only, and we must log every access. I can sign after I see the extraction plan.

tasha: I can run the redaction pipeline client-side before export to S3 so the export never contains raw PII. Proposed flow:
1) create ephemeral pod in acme VPC with read-only access to the log volume
2) run redaction script that replaces emails/ips/ssn-like tokens
3) push redacted output to `s3://redwood-incidents-acme-exception/1713103712/` with SSE-KMS
4) delete pod and mark bucket for 48h TTL

Here's the redaction command I'd run (example):

```
cat raw.log 
  | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/<email_redacted>/g' \
  | sed -E 's/([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/<ip_redacted>/g' \
  | jq '.request.headers |= {"x-correlation-id": .request.headers["x-correlation-id"]}' > redacted.log
```

anya: that flow sounds good. Customer is okay with client-side redaction if we can also provide a hash of original ids for correlation (not reversible).

miguel: will need permission for ephemeral pod creation in the Acme VPC and a short-lived IAM role that can write to the bucket. ops-bot can we create a short-lived role with the following policy? `s3:PutObject`, `s3:PutObjectAcl`, `kms:Encrypt`, resource limited to the exception prefix.

ops-bot: created incident-exception ticket INC-2024-ACME-457 and generated pre-signed bucket prefix `s3://redwood-incidents-acme-exception/1713103712/`. IAM role `incident-exception-acme` created with TTL 4h. Link: https://infra.internal/INC-2024-ACME-457

jane-legal: please include the justification text here. I'll prepare the formal exception document once I see the justification + the planned redaction script. Miguel/sarah: add who will access and the minimal data fields needed.

miguel: justification: to correlate `kv_cache_oom` sequence with full request payloads to reproduce and validate a fix for our kernel selection/runtime autoscale interaction. fields needed: request_id, timestamp, model, request_payload (masked), response_code, user_email (hashed), source_ip (redacted). Accessors: miguel (on-call), sarah (on-call-next), jane-legal.

jane-legal: ack. Preparing exception doc. @alex-ciso please sign this: https://legal.internal/exceptions/preview/INC-2024-ACME-457

alex-ciso: reviewed. signing conditional on tasha's redaction pipeline run and a recorded session for any manual inspections. I signed the doc; waiting on the redaction output and access log.

tasha: running pipeline now in ephemeral pod. ETA ~6m. Will post `redacted.log.gz` to the pre-signed prefix when done. Script will also produce SHA256s of original identifiers so we can correlate without exposing PII.

ops-bot: upload complete: `s3://redwood-incidents-acme-exception/1713103712/redacted.log.gz` (encrypted). Access logs will be retained and appended to INC-2024-ACME-457.

miguel: pulling redacted log now. Confirming the `kv_cache_oom` sequence — I can reproduce locally with a small trace. Patch queued to runtime canary, will deploy to one dedicated node.

sarah: taking the page from miguel now (handoff). Handoff notes: root cause looks like a degenerate sequence of long-context requests exceeding our adaptive KV cache heuristics; mitigation: bump kv_cache shard limit on acme pool, apply canary patch, monitor 15m.

jane-legal: exception signed and uploaded to ticket. Reminder: customer wants a letter confirming that raw PII was never exposed outside the encrypted exception store and that it will be destroyed within 48h.

miguel: confirmed — no human inspected raw PII; pipeline redacted before write. we'll push canary now.

tasha: canary applied. monitoring metrics: error rate dropped from 14% -> 0.7% on canary pod. continuing rollout to acme dedicated pool with gradual steps.

sarah: marking this thread as in-mitigation. Will create follow-up postmortem and include the exception approval docs. Closing the incident channel thread when rollout complete.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in progress. Owner: sarah. ETA post-deploy monitoring 1713114000. :white_check_mark:
